opt2: Shakespeare's will and testament has been the subject of much analysis.
opt3: Most people agree that Shakespeare was a very innovative writer.
opt4: Shakespeare wrote more plays than any other English playwright.
scan_comment: Negative item: three claims come from three different sentences of one paragraph
why1: Every word has been subjected to endless analysis
why2: The will's sentence generated widespread critical debate
why3: General consensus that he was the most innovative playwright

opt1: valuable
opt2: strange
opt3: detailed
opt4: generous
scan_comment: The synonym 'very detailed will' sits two sentences earlier in the same paragraph
why1: Borrows 'large and valuable' from the previous sentence
why2: Nothing marks the instructions as strange
why4: Generosity is not attributed to the instructions

stem: The main purpose of the third paragraph is to -
opt1: explain the symbolic meaning of the second-best bed
opt2: explain why Shakespeare spent most of his time in London
opt3: present Hathaway's reaction to Shakespeare's will
opt4: present one view of Shakespeare's bequest to his wife
scan_comment: Symbolism and the London detail are both evidence inside one scholarly reading
why1: The symbolism is one clause supporting the reading
why2: London is cited as evidence, never explained
why3: Hathaway's own reaction is never reported

stem: The last paragraph suggests that the second-best bed -
opt1: had been used by Shakespeare's guests
opt2: was always left to the widow
opt3: was a standard feature of wills at that time
opt4: meant more to Hathaway than the best bed
scan_comment: The marital-bed versus guest-bed sentence plus the sentimental framing is enough
why1: The best bed, not the second-best, was for guests
why2: The law concerned property generally, and 'always' overstates it
why3: Nothing about beds being standard in wills of the period

stem: The main purpose of the text is to -

opt2: present contrasting opinions of the global novel
opt3: describe an experiment in collaborative writing
opt4: present the benefits of global cooperation
scan_comment: Plot, process and verdict paragraphs must be summed into one description
why1: The heroine occupies part of the first paragraph
why2: Only Faber's mixed verdict is given; no opposing opinions
why4: One project's outcome is not a case for global cooperation

stem: According to the first paragraph, Maria Teresa Almendros -

opt4: is the hero of the global novel

why1: The fourteen authors devised the project, not the character
why2: The gods trouble the ancient hero; she seeks a lost father
why3: She is the character, not one of the writers

stem: According to the last paragraph, what did Michel Faber find surprising?
opt1: Authors from different countries have such similar writing styles.
opt2: There were political tensions among the authors.
opt3: The group of authors succeeded in writing a novel.
opt4: The book was well structured and believable.
scan_comment: His disappointment comes first; the miraculous-achievement line is at the very end
why1: Styles varied greatly and national clichés held true
why2: Political tension is what usually happens elsewhere, not here
why4: He says it lacks structure and emotional believability

stem: According to the second paragraph, unlike some other scholars, Touwaide -

why2: Compounds are what he hopes to prove, not prior knowledge
why3: True of him, but it is not the contrast with other scholars

stem: It can be inferred from the last paragraph that Touwaide is excited because -
